blocks.html: A WhatsApp API message template is a pre-approved message format that lets your business send proactive WhatsApp messages — order updates, OTPs, payment reminders, appointment confirmations and offers — to opted-in customers, even when they aren't actively chatting. You write the message once with placeholders like {{1}}, get it approved by Meta, and reuse it for thousands of customers with CTA buttons like Pay Now, Track Order or Call. For Indian businesses in 2026, templates are the difference between fast, consistent, compliant messaging and slow manual follow-ups that lose leads. This guide covers how templates work, the 24-hour rule, the three categories (Utility, Authentication, Marketing), naming and approval rules, why templates get rejected, and a copy-paste library you can customise and submit. New to the API itself? Start with WhatsApp Business App vs API.

sections.heading: What Is a WhatsApp API Message Template?

blocks.html: WhatsApp API message templates are the pre-approved, reusable messages businesses use to start conversations on the WhatsApp Business API. Unlike a normal chat reply, a template can be sent proactively to an opted-in customer at any time — which is exactly what makes WhatsApp work for automation, notifications and campaigns at scale.

You only fill in the small details (name, order ID, amount, date) via variables; the structure stays fixed and on-brand. If you're shortlisting a provider, run each one through our WhatsApp BSP checklist, and see the full WhatsApp Business API platform.

sections.heading: WhatsApp Template Categories in India (Utility, Authentication, Marketing)

blocks.html: Every template belongs to one category, and the category decides both how it's reviewed and what it costs. Since India moved to per-message pricing on 1 January 2026, marketing messages cost far more than utility or authentication, so correct categorisation directly affects your bill.

rows: Hi {{1}}, your order {{2}} is shipped. Delivery: {{3}}.

items.title: Categorise correctly to control cost:
items.desc: An order update is Utility (~₹0.115), not Marketing (~₹0.88). Mislabelling overpays. Rates are Meta base; add 18% GST and any BSP markup. For OTPs, see OTP & 2FA.

items.title: Don't mix intents:
items.desc: An order update must not carry "Buy 1 Get 1" — mixing promo into utility risks rejection and reclassification.

High-performing templates are built for speed: the customer should understand the message in three seconds and know the next step. The structure is simple — Header → Body → Variables → Buttons.

items.title: Header:
items.desc: A short context line ("Payment Reminder", "Order Shipped"), or a media header (image/video) for marketing.

items.title: Body:
items.desc: One purpose, short lines, a clear action — pay, confirm, track, visit or reply.

items.title: Variables:
items.desc: Placeholders like {{1}}, {{2}} insert name, order ID, amount or date, so one template serves thousands.

items.title: Buttons:
items.desc: One-tap CTAs — Pay Now, Track Order, Call Now, Get Directions, Book Now — lift conversions because customers don't type.

Body: Hi {{1}}, your payment of ₹{{2}} is due on {{3}}. Tap below to pay now.
Buttons: Pay Now | Call Support

blocks.html: Once you have 20+ templates, naming keeps your team fast and your approvals clean. Organise by industry + purpose, and write for clarity. Recommended format: industry_purpose_action_v1 — for example, realestate_sitevisit_reminder_v1, payments_due_reminder_v1, auth_login_otp_v1.

items.title: One intent per template:
items.desc: Never mix an update with an offer — keep Utility clean and offers in Marketing.

items.title: Simple language:
items.desc: Short lines, minimal punctuation, one clear CTA the customer grasps in 3 seconds.

items.title: Use variables naturally:
items.desc: {{1}} name, {{2}} order ID, {{3}} amount/date should read smoothly, with no awkward gaps.

items.title: Stay brand-safe and factual:
items.desc: Show your brand name and skip risky claims ("guaranteed", "100% returns") that trigger rejection.

sections.heading: Why WhatsApp Templates Get Rejected (and How to Pass)

blocks.html: Most rejections come down to a handful of avoidable issues. Fix these before you submit and approvals usually clear quickly.

items.title: Unclear intent:
items.desc: Vague text like "Important update" with no detail. Be specific about what and why.

items.title: Promo inside utility:
items.desc: Discounts or offers in a utility template get reclassified or rejected — keep them in Marketing.

items.title: Risky or misleading claims:
items.desc: "Guaranteed returns", "100% success", "no risk" — keep it factual.

items.title: Formatting issues:
items.desc: Broken variables, excessive punctuation or placeholder gaps. Keep it clean and consistent.

blocks.html: Here are ready-to-use templates you can customise and submit. Replace placeholders with real details: {{1}} = customer name, {{2}} = brand/order ID, {{3}} = amount/location, {{4}} = date/time.
Payment reminder (Utility)
Hi {{1}}, this is a reminder from {{2}}. Your payment of ₹{{3}} is due on {{4}}. Tap below to pay now or call us for help.
<small>Buttons: Pay Now | Call Support</small>
Appointment reminder (Utility)
Hi {{1}}, your appointment is scheduled on {{2}} at {{3}}. Reply 1 to confirm or 2 to reschedule.
Order shipped (Utility)
Hello {{1}}, your order {{2}} has been shipped. Expected delivery: {{3}}. Track your order below.
<small>Button: Track Order</small>
Login OTP (Authentication)
Your OTP for login is {{1}}. Valid for {{2}} minutes. Do not share it with anyone.
Password reset OTP (Authentication)
Use OTP {{1}} to reset your password. Expires in {{2}} minutes. If you didn't request this, please ignore.
Festival offer (Marketing)
Hi {{1}} 👋 Festival offer is live! Get {{2}}% off on {{3}}. Valid till {{4}}. Tap below to claim.
<small>Button: Claim Offer</small>
Re-engagement (Marketing)
Hi {{1}}, quick check-in from {{2}}. Do you still need help with {{3}}? Reply YES and we'll share the best options.

sections.heading: WhatsApp Template Messages vs Session Messages: What's the Difference

blocks.html: A common point of confusion is the difference between template messages and session (free-form) messages. Both are part of WhatsApp Business API, but they follow different rules — and getting this right keeps you compliant and controls your cost.
In short: templates are how you start or re-open a conversation; session messages are what you send once the customer is already talking to you.

rows: Anytime, to opted-in contacts (to start or re-open)
Only within 24 hrs of the customer's last message

items.title: Templates start the conversation:
items.desc: Use an approved template to reach a customer proactively or after the 24-hour window closes.

items.title: Session messages continue it:
items.desc: Once a customer replies, you can chat freely (text, media, buttons) for 24 hours — no template needed.

items.title: The window resets:
items.desc: Every new customer message restarts the 24-hour window, so timely replies keep messaging free-form.

items.title: Plan for cost:
items.desc: Templates are billed by category; session replies inside the window are free — design flows that keep conversations active.

blocks.html: Buttons are what turn a template from a notification into a conversion. WhatsApp supports several button types, and choosing the right one for each message lifts response rates because customers act in one tap instead of typing.

items.title: Quick reply buttons:
items.desc: Pre-set replies like "Confirm", "Reschedule" or "Yes" — ideal for appointments, confirmations and simple choices.

items.title: Call-to-action (URL) buttons:
items.desc: Send customers to a payment link, tracking page or booking form — great for "Pay Now", "Track Order" or "Book Now".

items.title: Call buttons:
items.desc: A one-tap dial button for support or sales — useful for high-value or urgent conversations.

items.title: Copy-code buttons:
items.desc: Used in authentication templates so customers can copy their OTP in one tap, reducing errors.

sections.heading: WhatsApp Quality Rating & Messaging Limits Explained

blocks.html: WhatsApp scores every business number with a quality rating based on how customers react to your messages. A healthy rating keeps your messaging limits high; a poor one can throttle how many customers you can reach. For high-volume Indian senders, protecting this rating is as important as the message itself.
Your number also sits in a messaging tier that caps how many business-initiated conversations you can start in 24 hours. Good quality and consistent volume unlock higher tiers automatically.

items.title: Quality rating (green / yellow / red):
items.desc: Based on blocks and reports — green keeps you scaling, red can pause your messaging.

items.title: Messaging tiers:
items.desc: Limits step up (1K → 10K → 100K → unlimited business-initiated conversations) as quality and volume grow.

items.title: What hurts your rating:
items.desc: Too many blocks or reports, irrelevant messaging, weak opt-in, or over-messaging.

items.title: How to protect it:
items.desc: Message only opted-in users, keep content relevant, control frequency, and use the right template category.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions: WhatsApp Business API Templates

items.q: What is a WhatsApp API message template?
items.a: A WhatsApp API message template is a pre-approved, reusable message format for sending proactive WhatsApp messages such as OTPs, order updates, reminders and offers to opted-in customers, with variables and CTA buttons.
When a customer messages you, you can reply freely for 24 hours. Outside that window, you must use an approved template to start or re-open the conversation.

items.q: What is the difference between Utility, Authentication and Marketing templates?
items.a: Utility templates are operational updates such as orders, payments and appointments. Authentication templates are OTPs and verification. Marketing templates are offers and re-engagement. The category affects both approval and per-message cost.

items.q: Why do WhatsApp templates get rejected?
items.a: Common causes are unclear intent, promotional content inside a utility template, risky or misleading claims, and formatting or variable errors. Keep copy simple, factual and single-intent.

items.q: How long does WhatsApp template approval take?
items.a: Clear, compliant templates are often approved within a few minutes to 24 hours. Vague or non-compliant templates take longer or get rejected.

items.q: Can I edit a WhatsApp template after it's approved?
items.a: You can edit templates, but changes usually require re-approval before the updated version can be sent. Use versioned names such as _v1 and _v2 to stay organised.

items.q: How much do WhatsApp template messages cost in India?
items.a: Pricing is per delivered message and varies by category. Marketing messages cost more than utility or authentication, and service replies inside the 24-hour window are free. Add 18% GST and any BSP markup. Contact Ojiva AI for current rates.
